en.headline: Hong Kong to pilot foreign domestic carers for elderly care next year
en.dek: The scheme, modelled on the existing foreign domestic helper regime, will admit carers with advanced training and experience to meet home-care needs of older residents.
body: Hong Kong will launch a pilot scheme next year to admit foreign domestic carers with more advanced training and experience in elderly care, Chief Executive John Lee announced in his Policy Address on Wednesday.
Lee said the arrangement would be modelled on the city’s existing regime for foreign domestic helpers and was intended to help meet the care needs of elderly persons living at home.

According to local reports, the pilot is expected to begin in 2027 with no fixed quota. Carers would need to complete relevant training in their home countries and possess several years of elderly-care experience; wages may be higher than those of standard foreign domestic helpers.

The measure forms part of a broader package of elderly-care initiatives that also includes expanding community and residential care service vouchers and adding new day-care and neighbourhood elderly centres.

zh.headline: 港府明年試行輸入外籍家居照顧員照顧長者
zh.dek: 行政長官在施政報告中宣布，參照外傭制度試行輸入具備較高護老培訓及經驗的外籍家居照顧員，以滿足居家長者照顧需要。
body: 行政長官李家超周三在《施政報告》中宣布，政府將於明年試行輸入具備較高護老技能培訓水平及經驗的外籍家居照顧員。
李家超表示，有關安排會參照現有輸入外籍家庭傭工制度，以滿足居家長者的照顧需要。
本地報道指，試行計劃預計2027年開始，暫不設配額，照顧員須在原居地接受相關培訓並具備數年護老經驗，薪酬水平可能高於一般外籍家庭傭工。
措施屬政府應對人口老化的一攬子計劃一部分，當中亦包括增加社區及院舍照顧服務券名額，以及增設日間護理中心及鄰舍長者中心。
